pass_b_english: He therefore rebukes the heavens and the earth most appropriately. For indeed He was going to make reproaches against Israel, and He wants the angels in heaven and also the whole earth to know the ways of that impious one, so that no one might think He moved in vain or might despise Him through small and trivial mistakes, by making the Beloved one rejected and His people set apart as His lot—the people of old who, through much strength, had been torn away from the greed of the Egyptians.

For He showed mercy indeed to those being wronged even against what was fitting, regarding the nobility that belonged to their fathers and was present in them, yet they had been treated with unthinking servitude.
Because indeed the greedy ones were acting in opposition, they were being punished bitterly, as God cast every kind of reproach upon them.
Just as therefore the reception of those from Israel has become highly significant, so He also intends that the manner of their rejection should not be unknown.

If indeed some were willing to have even these things called out by means of the voice of the prophet, the power of the meanings of the proper words would not have sinned against those to whom that had been revealed.
For Israel was indeed redeemed, as I have said, from the impiety of the Egyptians through Moses.

Because Pharaoh, opposing the divine signals with impiety, was saying, 'I do not know the Lord, and I will not send Israel,' he was being swept up by his own master against those whom the creation loathed.
For from above and from heaven are most of those things which have become glorious signs, and likewise many things in that land are both numerous and not uncommon.

For indeed the heaven cast down the hail, and the earth vomited forth frogs, just as it has been written (Exodus 8:2); and the water was being transformed into blood, and soot from furnaces was being scattered, and the air was thundering, with wounds and boils seething up; all these things happened to those among all creation.

Just as these very elements once labored upon the redeemed, 'Hear, O heaven,' he says, 'and be enlightened, O earth, because the Lord has spoken' (Isaiah 66:1). Yet we approach the meanings of the things foretold in a different way.

For the Israelites had dishonored the instruction given through the law, and having grown impatient with the saving lessons, they abandoned the one God who is by nature, turning instead to unclean demons. They sought healings in mountains and hills, and in the well-wooded ravines they offered incense and prostrated themselves before the works of their own hands.

And the God of all things was indignant at these things, and most appropriately so, and he said to one of the holy prophets: 'Arise and be judged against the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice' (Amos 1:2).
